clue.text: Sniper originally hits target, sprawling, most horizontal

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word sniper
sprawling suggests the letters of the two words are spread about into a new order

explanation.surface: A sniper's shot finds its mark and the victim falls flat on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sprawling' looks like a description of the fallen target, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something perfectly level is the least tilted, so the most horizontal line is the flattest and least bent.

clue.text: End of concert, then seat in club perhaps

indicators.note: End of picks out the final letter of the word concert

parts.note: the seat is the backside, also called the rump

explanation.surface: After the concert ends, someone takes a seat at their club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' looks like a social club, but it is the card suit; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: In a card game any suit, clubs included, can be named the winning suit that beats all others.

clue.text: Double parking in a Ranger docked permit

indicators.note: in puts the pair of letters inside the following words
docked means cut short, so the final letter of the word comes off

parts.note: a ranger is one who roams, a rover

indicators.note: Double asks for the letter for parking written two times

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A park ranger who double-parked has had a permit docked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double parking' reads as an offence, but 'Double' just repeats the parking letter; 'docked' cuts the tail off the ranger word.
explanation.definitionFit: To permit something is to allow or sanction it, giving official consent.

clue.text: Mineral aggregate under pressure below empty gantry

indicators.note: below sets the following pieces underneath the gantry's letters in this down entry
under places the aggregate beneath the pressure letter in the down light
empty leaves only the outside letters of the word gantry, its middle removed

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
an aggregate is a total, a sum

explanation.surface: Building aggregate, under strain, sits beneath an unloaded gantry on a construction site.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'under' and 'below' mean later: GY, then P, then SUM.
explanation.definitionFit: This soft white rock of calcium sulphate is a mineral used for plaster.

clue.text: Mountain's divided by burst streams

indicators.note: divided by means the hills' letters are split with the other piece placed in the gap

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, so the plural is read here as tors
a rent is a tear or split, something burst open

explanation.surface: A mountain is split by streams bursting down its sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burst' looks like a verb describing the streams, but it is a noun-like piece meaning a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: Torrents are violent, rushing flows of water, so they are fast streams.

clue.text: Putting aside row about nothing

indicators.note: about means the row's letters go around the other piece

parts.note: a row of beads or pearls is a string
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An argument over nothing gets shelved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' wants to be a quarrel; here it is a line of things, a string.
explanation.definitionFit: Storing goods means keeping them aside for later use, saving them up.

clue.text: Covert pursuit with sortie organised

indicators.note: organised suggests the letters of the two words are arranged into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A secret chase is mounted alongside a planned military raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges PURSUIT and SORTIE; 'with' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Covert and stealthy both describe something done secretly so as not to be noticed.

clue.text: Lord's adjudication coming from posh member — I fume

parts.note: U is the classic label for upper-class, posh usage
an MP is a Member of Parliament
to fume is to seethe, to rage

explanation.surface: A posh member of the Lord's club fumes at a cricket decision.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the famous London cricket ground; the decisions there come from the umpires.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruling on play at the cricket ground is the umpire's job, so the umpire's office is adjudication.

clue.text: Put off due to rain, spectator moved

indicators.note: moved suggests the letters of the two words are shifted into another order

explanation.surface: A match is called off because of rain, and the spectator goes home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put off' looks like a cancelled match; here it means to delay.
explanation.definitionFit: To procrastinate is to delay or postpone acting, putting a task off until later.

clue.text: Assume America in revolt with Republican getting in

parts.note: US stands for the United States, America

indicators.note: getting in means the party letter enters the middle of the revolt word

parts.note: people who have risen in revolt are said to be up in arms, or simply up

explanation.surface: America rebels as the Republican party takes office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' means risen in revolt, as in 'the people are up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To usurp power is to assume it wrongfully, taking a position by force.

clue.text: Some whimper for mercy seeing clown possibly

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A circus clown whimpers, pleading for mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'seeing', but that is only a link word joining wordplay to definition; 'clown possibly' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A clown is one example of an entertainer on stage or in the ring, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Duplicate ace needed in contract

indicators.note: needed in puts the expert inside the word for shrink

parts.note: to contract is to shrink or reduce
an ace is an expert, a pro

explanation.surface: A duplicate ace card is wanted for a game of contract bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' looks like a noun or the bridge game; it is the verb shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: To duplicate something is to copy it, making a replica.

clue.text: Initially it's learnt in anatomy, composition of bone

indicators.note: Initially takes the opening letter of each of the five words that follow

explanation.surface: A medical student learns the make-up of bone early in an anatomy course.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the ilium, the large pelvic bone, so it means belonging to that bone.

clue.text: Fathers about to be put in homes

indicators.note: to be put in means the short word for about goes inside the homes word

parts.note: pads are flats, slang for homes
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Elderly fathers are about to be moved into care homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'soon'; 'about' is RE, and 'to be put in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Padres are chaplains, and priests are addressed as Father.

clue.text: Ring road's shortly to circle area's dumps

parts.note: a disc is a flat round shape, a ring
A is the abbreviation for area
Rd is the short form of road, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: A ring road's being built around an area full of rubbish tips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dumps' looks like a noun; it is the verb, throws away.
explanation.definitionFit: To discard something is to throw it away, to get rid of it.

clue.text: Spots magistrate thundering about scrapping R.E.

indicators.note: thundering about suggests the letters rushing around noisily into a new order
scrapping means the named letters are thrown out of the word first

parts.note: RE is the school subject Religious Education

explanation.surface: A magistrate thunders on about scrapping religious education in schools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrapping' removes R and E from MAGISTRATE, leaving MAGISTAT, which 'thundering about' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Stigmata are marks or blemishes on the skin, spots like those said to mirror Christ's wounds.

clue.text: Reputation of hog with energy eating remains

indicators.note: eating means the animal word takes the leftovers inside it

parts.note: a hog is a pig
the remains are the rest
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An energetic hog gobbles up the leftover scraps.
explanation.definitionFit: Prestige is standing or renown, the esteem in which someone is held.

clue.text: Dangerous current spot occupied by mongrel

parts.note: in means fashionable, current

indicators.note: occupied by means the dog word sits inside the sighting word

parts.note: to spot is to see
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A mongrel has taken over a spot near a dangerous current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like a flow of water or electricity; it is the adjective, fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsafe or risky, a structure that is not firmly fixed is dangerous.

clue.text: Clubs with old band covering Queen set

parts.note: C is the card abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: covering means the band's letters wrap around the queen's

parts.note: a tie is a band or cord that binds
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Clubs with an old dance band put on a set for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive group, a set of people sharing interests.

clue.text: Church followers start to talk getting stick

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a leader's men are followers

indicators.note: start to picks the opening letter of the word talk

explanation.surface: A church congregation starts talking and gets a stick from the vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick' looks like a noun or criticism; it is the verb, glue.
explanation.definitionFit: To cement two things is to bind them firmly, making them stick together.

clue.text: Former partner reportedly stalked in passage

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word heard rather than written

parts.note: to stalk prey is to have tracked it

explanation.surface: A former partner was said to have stalked someone, according to a newspaper passage.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract is a short excerpt, a passage taken from a book or text.

clue.text: Exhibitionist rose up flashing

indicators.note: flashing suggests the letters darting about into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A flasher stood up and exposed himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flashing' fits the exhibitionist picture, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser shows off to impress, behaving like an exhibitionist seeking attention.

clue.text: Snooze during sex is not appropriate

indicators.note: during means the snooze sits inside the other word

parts.note: it is slang for sex or sex appeal
a snooze is a nap

explanation.surface: Nodding off in the middle of sex is not the done thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable, so something not appropriate for the occasion.

clue.text: Rower perhaps left in ship by crew

indicators.note: in places the side word inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS is short for steamship
port is the left-hand side of a ship
to crew a boat is to man it

explanation.surface: A rower is left behind in a ship by the rest of the crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower competing in races is one kind of athlete, hence 'perhaps' as an example.

clue.text: Tough male with a cut, not keeping quiet

indicators.note: not keeping means the quiet letter is dropped from the cut

parts.note: a chop is a cut or blow
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A tough guy with a cut on his face keeps quiet no longer.
explanation.definitionFit: Macho describes aggressively masculine, tough-guy behaviour.

clue.text: Bounder's idea to pinch bottom

indicators.note: to pinch means the words grip the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A cad thinks it fun to pinch someone's bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinch bottom' paints the cad's groping; 'to pinch' is the hidden-word signal. A bounder is an old-fashioned British word for a cad.
explanation.definitionFit: The underside is the lower surface of something, its bottom.

clue.text: Coat's unbuttoned revealing necktie

indicators.note: unbuttoned suggests the coat's letters loosened and undone into a new order

explanation.surface: Opening a coat shows off the necktie underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Coat's' supplies an S for the fodder. The tie takes its name from Royal Ascot, the English racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascot is a broad neckcloth or cravat, a kind of tie worn at formal events.

clue.text: Role with cabinet reshuffles in party

indicators.note: reshuffles suggests the letters, like ministers, being moved into new positions

explanation.surface: A prime minister reshuffles the cabinet roles at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebration is a festive gathering, a party held to mark an occasion.
